newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia January palm oil exports, output seen down.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia January palm oil exports, output seen down.

text.p: Indonesian palm oil exports totalled some 170,000 tonnes in January, compared with 180,000 tonnes in December, traders said on Friday.
They said crude palm oil production fell to around 370,000 tonnes in January from an estimated 380,000 tonnes in December.
They said output at some plantations fell by up to 10 percent.

"Production in my plantation in North Sumatra was below expectations, falling by some six percent," one senior trader told Reuters. "There has been a slight improvement in February production, but the final numbers are not in yet."
"Production depends on the individual plantations...their location, management and maturity of trees," he said.
Another trader said his plantation, also on the island of Sumatra where most of the country's oil palm plantations are located, saw production falling by 10 percent in January.
"The drop in production in January was less than in December," he said. "I think we will be seeing some improvement in production in February."
Traders said there had been a decline in Indonesian crude palm oil output since the third quarter of last year due to seasonal and weather-related reasons.
"Last year we did not have a peak season because of bad weather," one trader said.
"Production in government-owned plantations was apparently affected by a shortage of fertilisers last year. I think production should begin to pick up from March," he added.
Traders said exports were generally stable in January, compared to December on the back of steady demand in Europe.
"Although the export taxes were relatively high, exports were good in January and could improve in February," he said.
Traders said tight crude palm oil supply had forced shipment delays in the Sumatran ports of Belawan and Dumai.
